<response>Idania, I understand how unsettling it is to experience persistent physical sensations when nothing is visibly causing them. In high-stress leadership roles, the body can sometimes react to anxiety or physiological fatigue in ways that feel like external intrusions, even when damage hasn't occurred. Given your role in managing crisis situations, you know that relying on evidence-based reality is vital for clear outcomes. My advice is to trust medical professionals as your source of facts; they can assess objective markers like nerve sensitivity or lipid metabolism that often explain these feelings without needing to look beyond biological function.

Please prioritize a consultation with a healthcare provider to get a clear picture of what is happening. That verification is the best way to regain your clarity and ensure you have the physical wellbeing needed to support others effectively.</response>
